children.translated_text: Gold, silver, red copper, lead, tin, and sharp iron

children.text: dhātavaḥ sapta vijñeyā aṣṭamaḥ kvāpi pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be known as the seven metals; mercury is in some places the eighth.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāraṃ ca tāmraṃ ca vaṅgo nāgastu pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, tin, and lead as the fifth,

children.text: rītikā ca tathā ghoṣo lohaṃ cetyaṣṭa dhātavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: also brass, bell-metal, and iron: these are the eight metals.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre kāñjike ca kulatthake
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow's urine, sour gruel, and horse gram decoction,
by being heated and quenched seven times, every metal becomes purified.
Gold has the appearance of the color of the campaka flower; silver and copper become blackish.
Bronze should be gray in color, and lead has the appearance of a pigeon.
Tin attains whiteness; sharp iron is like the fruit of the jambu tree.
Mica should have the appearance of a brick: this is the determination of the colors of the metals.
When the seven metals are combined with realgar, latex of arka, and sulfur,

children.text: puṭaiśca dvādaśaiḥ paraṃ vrajanti bhasmatāṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: through twelve heating operations they always afterwards reach the state of bhasma.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham
children.translated_text: In heating it is red, in cutting white, and on the touchstone like saffron;
produced from silver and copper, unctuous, soft: such gold is the best and very heavy.

children.text: śvetāṅgaṃ kaṭhinaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ samalaṃ dalam
children.translated_text: That which has a whitish body, is hard, dry, discolored, impure, and flaky,

children.text: dāhe chede sitaṃ śvetaṃ kaṣe laghu ca tattyajet ||
children.translated_text: white in heating and cutting, white on the touchstone, and light: that should be rejected.
The best gold, melted in fire, should be cast thirty times
into the juices of kancanara; the gold becomes thoroughly purified.
When the gold is melted, one should add lead in the proportion of a sixteenth part.

children.text: cūrṇayitvā tathāmlena ghṛṣṭvā kṛtvā ca golakam ||
children.translated_text: Having pulverized it, then rubbed it with sour liquid, and made it into a pellet,
one should add sulfur equal to the pellet, above and below,
place it in a closed pair of earthen saucers, and heat it with twenty forest cow-dung cakes.
Thus, with seven heating operations, gold becomes non-revivable bhasma.
Or lead ash, equal to the gold leaf and smeared with lemon juice,

children.text: trivāraṃ vai gajapuṭe suvarṇaṃ bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: when heated three times in a gajaputa, makes gold attain the state of bhasma.
Or the gold leaves should be smeared with the excrement of pigeons or with that produced by fowls.
The gold leaves are to be smeared, and layer after layer should be applied.
Having made an equal amount of powdered sulfur, in a closed vessel joined from earthen saucers,
one should apply a kukkutaputa with five cow-dung cakes.
In this way one should give nine heating operations, and the tenth should be a great heating.
It should be given with thirty forest cow-dung cakes; then gold bhasma is produced.

children.text: svarṇaṃ śītaṃ pavitraṃ kṣayavamikasanaśvāsamehāsrapittakṣaiṇyakṣveḍakṣatāsrapradaragadaharaṃ svādu tiktaṃ kaṣāyam
children.translated_text: Gold is cooling and purifying; it removes consumption, vomiting, cough, asthma, urinary disease, blood and pitta disorders, wasting, poison, wounds, bleeding, and vaginal discharge; it is sweet, bitter, and astringent.

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ medhāgnikāntipradamadhurasaraṃ kārśyahāri tridoṣonmādāpasmāraśūlajvarajayi vapuṣo bṛṃhaṇaṃ netrapathyam ||
children.translated_text: It is aphrodisiac, gives intelligence, digestive fire, and complexion, has sweet essence, removes emaciation, conquers the three doṣas, insanity, epilepsy, colic, and fever, nourishes the body, and is beneficial to the eyes.

children.text: etad bhasma suvarṇajaṃ madhughṛtopetaṃ dviguñjonmitaṃ līḍhaṃ hanti nṛṇāṃ kṣayāgnisadanaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsārucī
children.translated_text: This bhasma born of gold, licked with honey and ghee in a measure of two guñjās, destroys in men consumption, weakness of digestive fire, asthma, cough, and loss of appetite.

children.text: ojodhātuvivardhanaṃ balakaraṃ pāṇḍvāmayadhvaṃsanaṃ pathyaṃ sarvaviṣāpahaṃ gadaharaṃ duṣṭagrahaṇyādihṛt ||
children.translated_text: It increases ojas and the bodily tissues, gives strength, destroys anemia, is wholesome, removes all poisons, cures diseases, and removes disorders such as faulty grahaṇī.

children.text: balaṃ ca vīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajān poṣayatīha kāye
children.translated_text: Improperly prepared gold takes away the strength and virility of men, and here in the body it nourishes multitudes of diseases.

children.text: asaukhyakāryeva sadaiva hemāpakvaṃ sadoṣaṃ maraṇaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Always producing discomfort, gold that is uncooked and defective causes death.

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇadalaṃ samastaviṣahṛcchūlāmlapittāpahaṃ hṛdyaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ kṣayavraṇaharaṃ kāyāgnimāndyaṃ jayet
children.translated_text: Purified gold leaf removes all poisons, colic, and sour-pitta disorder; it is good for the heart, nourishing, removes consumption and wounds, and conquers weakness of the bodily digestive fire.

children.text: hikkānāhaharaṃ paraṃ kaphaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ hitaṃ sarvadā tattadrogaharānupānasahitaṃ sarvāmayadhvaṃsanam ||
children.translated_text: It removes hiccup and abdominal distension, is supremely kapha-removing, always beneficial to men, and, accompanied by the appropriate vehicle for each disease, destroys every illness.

children.text: guru snigdhaṃ mṛdu śvetaṃ dāhe chede ca yatkṣamam
children.translated_text: That which is heavy, unctuous, soft, white, and withstands heating and cutting,
excellent in color and clear like the moon: silver here is endowed with virtues.
Artificial silver is hard, dry, with leaves red and yellow, and light;

children.text: dāhe chede ca yannaṣṭaṃ rūpye doṣā daśa smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that which is ruined in heating and cutting: ten defects are remembered in silver.
Silver, made into leaves and well heated in fire,
is pure when quenched three times in the juice of Agastya.
Having made the silver leaves thin, separately with equal quantities
of mercury and sulfur, and with equal orpiment, placed in a mortar,
one should make a paste with the water of aloe and smear those leaves with it.
Sealed in a pair of earthen saucers, it should be heated with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.
Thus silver indeed attains death, that is, calcination, with two such operations.
Having prepared an amalgam with mercury, one should then mix it with the silver.
Afterwards one should triturate equal amounts of orpiment and sulfur with lemon juice.
With two or three heating operations it becomes bhasma; this should be used in rasādi preparations.
One should heat fine heaps of silver leaves soaked in pyrite, realgar, and lemon juice.

children.text: dvitrivāramatha bhasmatāṃ vrajet pātakaugha iva śaṅkarasmṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: After two or three times it reaches the state of bhasma, like a mass of sins at the remembrance of Śaṅkara.

children.text: tāraṃ śītakaṣāyamamlamadhuraṃ doṣatrayacchedanaṃ snigdhaṃ dīpanamakṣikukṣigadajiddāhaṃ viṣādiṃ haret
children.translated_text: Silver is cooling, astringent, sour, and sweet; it cuts through the three doṣas, is unctuous, kindles digestion, conquers diseases of the eyes and belly, and removes burning and poisons and the like.

It breaks up fat, counteracts intoxication and its excess, produces complexion, life span, and health, and, being mobile, destroys consumption, loss of memory, colic, anemia, gray hair, spleen disease, and fever.
Impure silver would cause anemia, itching, and stiffness of the throat,
constipation, loss of virility, loss of strength, and headache.
They say poison is not poison; copper, however, is called poison.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvaṣṭau doṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is one defect in poison, but in copper eight defects are proclaimed.
Dizziness, fainting, burning, sweating, moistening, and vomiting,
loss of appetite and mental distress: these defects are like poison.
Therefore one should thoroughly purify copper for the removal of those defects.
One should smear a copper sheet with the milk of the vajri plant mixed with salt.
After heating it in fire, one should sprinkle it three times with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Or, by sprinklings with the milky sap of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, purification of copper is produced.
One should cook a copper sheet in cow urine for one yāma with a strong fire.
With acidic alkali, copper attains complete purification in every way.
One should triturate powder of purified copper with an equal amount of mercury,
in a mortar with citron juice, and sulphur equal to those two.
Cooked for a day in a gajapuṭa, copper bhasma is produced.
One should smear copper sheets with the juices of sesame leaves.
They quickly become bright in color; no deliberation is needed here.
Sheets of purified copper, measuring two śuktis,

children.text: trapu śuktimitaṃ tena veṣṭayitvātha tāni tu ||
children.translated_text: and tin measuring one śukti: after wrapping those with it,

children.text: yāmaṃ paced ghaṭīyantre yadā trapumayaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: one should cook them for a yāma in a ghaṭī apparatus. When it has become tin-like,
one should remove it when self-cooled and eat it in a dose measuring one valla.
With drying agents of ginger and yavakṣāra,
this tin-copper immediately destroys disorders of kapha, anorexia, and spleen disease.
With mercury equal to the copper, with an equal amount of strong sulphur,
with orpiment half of that portion, and with realgar half of that,
having made a smooth kajjalī, resembling very fine collyrium,
one should smear the copper sheets alternately with the kajjalī.
One should cook it in the sand apparatus prescribed in the chapter on apparatuses,
and cook it thoroughly for two yāmas; when self-cooled, one should take it out.

children.text: tattadrogaharānupānasahitaṃ tāmraṃ dvivallonmitaṃ tallīḍhaṃ pariṇāmaśūlamudaraṃ śūlaṃ ca pāṇḍujvaram
children.translated_text: This copper, in a dose of two vallas, licked together with an appropriate vehicle that removes each particular disease, removes pariṇāma-śūla, abdominal disease, colic, anemia, and fever.

children.text: gulmaplīhakṣayāgnisādasadanaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsaṃ tathā duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ hareddhruvamidaṃ tatsomanāthābhidham ||
children.translated_text: It also surely removes abdominal lumps, spleen disease, wasting, weakness of digestive fire, debility, dyspnea, cough, and bad grahaṇī disease. This is called <s>Somanātha</s>.

children.text: nepālaṃ samarudrabījam asuras tulyas tayos tālakas tasyārdhārdhaśilāṃ vidhāya vidhinā ślakṣṇāṃ parāṃ kajjalīm
children.translated_text: Taking nepāla, with marudbīja, asura, and orpiment equal to those two, and realgar equal to half and half of that, one should properly make a very smooth, excellent kajjalī.

children.text: liptvā tāmradalānyadhordhvamanayā bhāṇḍe pacedyāmakaṃ yantrādhyāyasamuktaśāstravidhinā tatsvāṅgaśītaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared copper leaves above and below with this, one should cook them in a vessel for a yāma according to the rule stated in the science in the chapter on apparatuses; when self-cooled, one should remove it.

children.text: tāmraṃ śītaṃ nihanyād vraṇakṛmijaṭharānāhasaṃplīhapāṇḍuśvāsaṃśleṣmāsravātakṣayapavanagadaṃ śūlayugmaṃ ca gulmam
children.translated_text: Copper, when cooled, destroys wounds, worms, abdominal disorders, distension, spleen disease, anemia, dyspnea, phlegm, bleeding, wasting caused by vāta, diseases of wind, the two kinds of colic, and abdominal lumps.

children.text: kuṣṭhānyaṣṭādaśāpi smarabalarucikṛdraktamedo'mlapittacchedi proktaṃ tvaśuddhaṃ krimim udaragadādhmānakuṣṭhādi kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: It is said to remove even the eighteen skin diseases, to produce sexual strength and appetite, and to cut off disorders of blood, fat, and acid pitta; but when unpurified it causes worms, abdominal disease, distension, skin disease, and the like.
Rītikā is to be known as twofold; among them the first is rājarītikā.
The second is kākatuṇḍī; of the two, the first is superior in qualities.
When heated and thrown into sour gruel, copper becomes rājarītikā.

children.text: kākatuṇḍī tu kṛṣṇā syānnāsau sevyā vijānatā ||
children.translated_text: But kākatuṇḍī is black; one who knows should not use it.
Kāṃsya too is said to be twofold, divided into puṣpa and tailika.
Among these, puṣpa is very white, while tailika has a tawny luster.
Of these two the first is best and should be used for the pacification of disease.
The physician should purify rājarīti and likewise ghoṣa as he does copper.
Their māraṇa too is declared by the best physicians to be like that of copper.
The pair of rītikās is dry, slightly bitter, salty, mobile,
purifying, destructive of anemia, destructive of worms, scraping, and cooling.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ viśadaṃ saram
children.translated_text: Kāṃsya is astringent, bitter, hot, scraping, clear, and mobile,

children.text: rūkṣaṃ guru ca cakṣuṣyaṃ kaphapittaharaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: dry and heavy, beneficial for the eyes, and supremely removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā kāntamiti lohaṃ tridhā smṛtam
children.translated_text: Iron is remembered as threefold: muṇḍa, tīkṣṇa, and kānta.
Tīkṣṇa is a hundred times superior to muṇḍa, and kānta is a hundred times superior to tīkṣṇa.

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tu vartulaṃ bhūmau parvateṣu ca jāyate
children.translated_text: Muṇḍa is round and is produced in the earth and in mountains.
Tīkṣṇa is such as gajabali and the like, and kānta is born from magnet-stone.

children.text: yatrāṅgaṃ dṛśyate lohe tīkṣṇaṃ lohaṃ taduttamam
children.translated_text: Where one's limb is seen in iron, that tīkṣṇa iron is excellent.
When iron is anointed with a paste of kāsīsa and āmalaka, one's face is seen in it.

children.text: yatpātrasthe prasarati jale tailabindurna datto hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: That in a vessel of which a drop of oil spreads over the water, asafoetida gives off its own smell, and neem paste its bitterness,

children.text: pācyaṃ dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmiṃ dagdhāṅgāḥ syuḥ sajalacaṇakāḥ kāntalohaṃ taduktam ||
children.translated_text: and milk cooked in it becomes shaped like a peak and does not fall to the ground, and wet chickpeas become burnt: that is said to be kānta iron.
A leaf of iron, smeared with hare's blood and somewhat with the milky sap of arka,
is blown in the fire and sprinkled with triphalā water.

children.text: evaṃ triśaḥ kṛte lohaṃ śuddhim āpnotyasaṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: When this is done three times, the iron undoubtedly attains purification.
Triphalā, sixteen palas, should be decocted in eight times as much water.
When in that decoction one quarter remains, five palas of iron,
made into sheets and heated, should be quenched seven times.
In this way the mountain-born metal, arisen as iron, dissolves.
For all irons, the best māraṇa is with rasa-bhasma.
The middling method is with herbs, and the lowest with sulphur and the like.
Of purified king mercury take one part, and of sulphur two parts.
Powder of iron, equal to the two, should be triturated with the juice of kanyakā.
For two yāmas; its ball should be wrapped with castor leaves,
then tied with thread and placed in a copper crucible.
One should seal its mouth with clay, dry it, and then again
keep it for three days in a heap of grain; after taking it out, one should triturate it.
That dust, strained through cloth, floats on water like a swan.
This iron bhasma is proclaimed under the name <s>Somāmṛta</s>.
One should mix darada, in a twelfth part, with the powder of tīkṣṇa iron,
and triturate it with the juice of kanyā for two yāmas; then again,
having placed it in a sealed pair of earthen saucers, one should heat it with a gajapuṭa.
Iron powder prepared seven times in this way becomes vāritara, floating on water.

children.text: lohacūrṇaṃ palaṃ khalve sārakasya palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One pala of iron powder in a mortar, and likewise one pala of sāraka,
and also one pala of aśvagandhā: all should be triturated together.
Afterwards, for a day, with the water of kumārī; then the ball, with rubu leaves,

children.text: saṃveṣṭya ca mṛdā liptvā puṭedgajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: should be wrapped, smeared with clay, and cooked by heating in a gajapuṭa.
When it has cooled of itself, one should take it out: the iron-dust is like sindūra.
One should take it as dead, vāritara iron; it is supreme, accomplishing every purpose.
Iron powder should be impregnated with juices produced from pomegranate leaves,
seven times in the sun; with that, again, two gajapuṭa heatings are given.

children.text: itthaṃ kṛtaṃ ca tadbhasma śuddhaṃ vāritaraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Bhasma made in this manner becomes pure and vāritara.
One should apply it in all diseases; this is true, as the guru's word declares.

children.text: gṛhītvā tīkṣṇajaṃ cūrṇaṃ tathaiva ca gavāṃ dadhi
children.translated_text: Taking powder made from tīkṣṇa iron, and likewise cow's curds,
one should prepare them together in a vessel until they reach dryness.
After taking it out, one should melt it in fire; three puṭas of triphalā

children.text: deyaṃ vāritaraṃ sadyo jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be given. It immediately becomes vāritara; there is no doubt about this.
One part of iron powder, and an equal amount of navasāgara,

children.text: kiṃcittaptodakaṃ grāhyaṃ sarvaṃ vastre nibadhya ca ||
children.translated_text: with a little hot water taken, should all be tied in cloth.
At the end of a yāma one should rub it in the hand; it immediately becomes vāritara.
One should apply it in all diseases, so that all diseases do not arise.
All this dead iron should be blown in the fire with the five allies.
In this way it becomes nirutthāna; it should be used when it is vāritara.
Honey, jaggery, ghee, guñjā, and ṭaṅkaṇa are the five allies.
With raktikā and ghee, joined with lākṣā, mixed with honey, and furnished with ṭaṅkaṇa,

children.text: ūrṇayā tathā dhmātatāṃ gatāḥ saptadhātavo yānti jīvatām ||
children.translated_text: and likewise with wool, the seven metals, having been subjected to blowing in the fire, attain living power.

children.text: gandhakaṃ cotthitaṃ lohaṃ tulyaṃ khalve vimardayet
children.translated_text: Sulphur and raised iron, in equal measure, should be triturated in a mortar.
For one day, with liquids of kanyā, then, having sealed it, one should cook it in a gajapuṭa.
In this manner the nirutthita preparation is to be made for all metals.

children.text: kāntaṃ tu śītaṃ madhuraṃ kaṣāyamāyuṣkaraṃ dhātuvivardhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Kānta iron is cooling, sweet, astringent, life-promoting, and increasing the bodily tissues.
It destroys the three doṣas, wounds, urinary disease, skin disease, spleen disease, abdominal disease, tumors, poison, and worms.

children.text: pāṇḍuṃ pīḍayati kṣayaṃ kṣapayati kṣaiṇyaṃ kṣiṇoti kṣaṇāt kāsaṃ nāśayati bhramaṃ śamayati śleṣmāmayān khādati
children.translated_text: It afflicts anemia, destroys wasting, removes emaciation in a moment, destroys cough, calms dizziness, and devours phlegmatic disorders.

children.text: asraṃ gulmasaśūlapīnasavamiśvāsapramehārucīr āśūnmūlayati prakampanaharaṃ lohaṃ himaṃ cākṣuṣam ||
children.translated_text: Iron that is cooling and good for the eyes quickly uproots disorders of blood, abdominal lumps with colic, coryza, vomiting, dyspnea, urinary disease, and anorexia, and it removes trembling.

children.text: śuddhaṃ pittakaphānilamohaṃ hanti hitaṃ śivaśaktyā loham
children.translated_text: When purified, iron destroys bewilderment from pitta, kapha, and anila, and is beneficial through auspicious power.
It is said to destroy anemia, disease, and pain; when unpurified, it develops diseases.

children.text: ye guṇā mṛtarūpyasya te guṇāḥ kāntabhasmanaḥ
children.translated_text: The qualities that dead silver has are the qualities of kānta-bhasma.
In the absence of kānta, silver should be given; so says <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājikāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Kūṣmāṇḍa, sesame oil, food of māṣa beans, and also mustard,
wine and sour tastes: one who uses iron should avoid them.
Fish, jīvaka, eggplant, māṣa, and bitter gourd,
exercise, pungent substances, wine, oil, and sour substances he should keep far away.
One should administer one valla, or a half-valla measure, as appropriate.
Triphalā and iron powder destroy wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: vyoṣaṃ bhārgī ca madhunā lohaṃ dhāturujāpaham
children.translated_text: Vyoṣa, bhārgī, and iron with honey remove pain in the bodily tissues.
With kajjalī, honey, and kṛṣṇā, it prevents phlegmatic diseases.
Sugar and caturjāta remove the pain of raktapitta.
Punarnavā with cow's milk is supreme for increasing strength.
With the juice of punarnavā itself, it destroys anemia.

children.text: haridrā lohacūrṇaṃ ca pippalī madhunā saha
children.translated_text: Haridrā, iron powder, and pippalī together with honey
destroy the twenty kinds of prameha; there is no doubt about this.
Joined with śilājatu, it prevents difficult urination.

children.text: vāsakaḥ pippalī drākṣā lohaṃ ca madhunā saha ||
children.translated_text: Vāsaka, pippalī, drākṣā, and iron together with honey:
one should eat the pill in the morning; it prevents the five kinds of cough.
Joined with betel, one should eat excellent iron.
It kindles the digestive fire, is aphrodisiac, and increases the body's luster.
What more need be said here? It is regarded as making the body like iron.
Iron powder that is deficient through too little medicine and too few puṭas, lacking sulphur and mercury,
and uncooked, causes a loss of lifespan for people.
The best kiṭṭa is a hundred years old; the middling is eighty years old.
The inferior is sixty years old; anything less than that is like poison.

children.text: akṣāṅgārair dhamet kiṭṭaṃ lohajaṃ tadgavāṃ jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: One should blow iron kiṭṭa with akṣa charcoal, and with cow's liquid
sprinkle it inside an akṣa vessel seven times, again and again.
Then, after powdering it, with decoctions produced from triphalā in double quantity,

children.text: āloḍya bharjayed vahnau maṇḍūraṃ jāyate varam ||
children.translated_text: one should stir it and roast it over fire; excellent maṇḍūra is produced.
Maṇḍūra is cooling, appetizing, and conquers anemia, swelling, and inflammation.
It conquers halīmaka, jaundice, spleen disease, and kumbha-jaundice.
Vaṅga is said to be twofold: khuraka and miśraka.

children.text: khuraṃ tatra guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na hitaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Among these, khura is superior in qualities; miśraka is considered not beneficial.
White, soft, smooth, melting quickly, and heavy:
that is khura-vaṅga, without sound; miśraka is dark and whitish.
After melting it, when it has been put into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s> mixed with night,
the <s>khura-vaṅga</s> is purified by three repetitions; there is no doubt.
The <s>vaṅga</s> should be of the measure of a <s>śāṇa</s>; the serpent-substance is desired in the measure of a <s>raktikā</s>.
When everything has melted in a potsherd, one should rub it with an iron ladle.
In one watch it becomes <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash), resembling split collyrium.
That <s>bhasma</s> becomes white through the intense fire of the potsherd.
One should smear sheets of <s>vaṅga</s> with the liquid of <s>palāśa</s>.

children.text: tālena puṭitaṃ bhasma trivāraṃ jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: When fired with <s>tāla</s>, the <s>bhasma</s> is certainly produced by three repetitions.
<s>Vaṅga</s>, smeared with oil of <s>bhallāta</s> and wrapped in cloth,
comes to destruction in a fire of tamarind, pippala, and palāśa wood.
When <s>vaṅga</s> has been melted in an earthen vessel, the powder of tamarind and aśvattha bark,
amounting to a fourth part, should be added again and again, and it should be stirred with an iron ladle.
Then, in the measure of two watches, <s>vaṅga-bhasma</s> is produced.
Next, having added <s>tāla</s> equal to the <s>bhasma</s>, one should triturate it with sour liquid.
Then, after cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (large pit-firing), one should again triturate it with sour liquid.
Thereafter one should fire it for one watch with <s>tāla</s> in a tenth part.

children.text: evaṃ daśapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ vaṅgaṃ tu mriyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, cooked with ten firings, <s>vaṅga</s> is certainly killed, that is, calcined.
<s>Vaṅga</s> is bitter, hot, dry, and slightly aggravating to <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys urinary disease, phlegmatic disorders, fat, and worms.
Unpurified <s>vaṅga</s>, though like nectar when purified, produces diseases such as <s>prameha</s>.
It produces abdominal tumors, heart disease, colic, piles, cough, dyspnea, and vomiting.
What melts quickly, is very heavy, black when cut, and shining,
with a foul smell and black externally, is purified <s>sīsa</s>; otherwise it is different.
<s>Nāga</s> (lead), melted by contact with fire and dropped into <s>ravidugdha</s>,
placed in a perforated pot, obtains purification by three repetitions.
Ash of aśvattha and tamarind bark, in a fourth part of the <s>nāga</s>,
should be cast onto the <s>nāga</s>; one should cook it in a vessel and stir it with an iron spoon.
After a watch, one should take up that <s>bhasma</s>, and with <s>manaḥśilā</s> equal to the <s>bhasma</s>,

children.text: jambīrairāranālair vā piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: having ground it with citron juice or with sour gruel, one should seal it and cook it in a firing.
When it has cooled by itself, one should grind it again, furnished with a twentieth part of <s>śilā</s>.
With sour liquid alone for one watch, one should cook it in a firing as before.
Thus, cooked by sixty firings, <s>nāga</s> becomes well deprived of its rising power.
A sheet of <s>nāga</s>, smeared and rubbed with <s>manaḥśilā</s>, sulphur, and <s>vāṭarūṣa</s>,

children.text: puṭaistribhiḥ kumbhamitaiḥ prayāti bhasmatvam etat pravadanti tajjñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with three pot-sized firings, attains the state of <s>bhasma</s>; those who know declare this.
By repeated coatings of <s>śilā</s> ground with the juice of betel,
<s>Nāga</s> certainly becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-revivifiable) through thirty-two firings.
<s>Sīsaka</s> is very hot, unctuous, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
It destroys <s>prameha</s> and disorders of water, stimulates digestion, and lessens <s>āmavāta</s>.
Unpurified <s>nāga</s> causes <s>prameha</s>, wasting, and jaundice.
Therefore only when thoroughly purified should it be calcined by the best physicians.

children.text: abhrakaṃ mākṣikaṃ tālaṃ śilā nīlāñjanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>śilā</s>, blue collyrium,
<s>tutthaka</s> and <s>rasaka</s> are said to be the seven subsidiary metals.

children.text: śuklaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ caiva yathākramam
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, and black respectively,

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: they are fourfold: <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajra</s>.

children.text: dalāni muñcatyanale pinākaṃ bhekaṃ svarāvaṃ kurute'nalastham
children.translated_text: The <s>pināka</s> releases flakes in the fire; the frog-like one makes a sound when placed in the fire.

children.text: phūtkāraṃ rāvaṃ bhujagaḥ karoti hyavikriyaṃ vahnigataṃ suvajram ||
children.translated_text: The serpent-like one makes a hissing sound, while the excellent diamond-like one remains unchanged when put into fire.
<s>Pināka</s> produces skin disease; <s>dardura</s> gives death.
<s>Nāga</s> may cause fistula, but diamond-like <s>abhraka</s> conquers a host of diseases.
<s>Abhraka</s>, heated red-hot and thrown seven times into sour gruel,

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ jāyate nūnaṃ prakṣiptaṃ vāpi gojale
children.translated_text: certainly becomes free from defects; or it may be thrown into cow's water,
or into a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, and especially into cow's milk.
One should blow black <s>abhraka</s> in the fire and then cast it into milk.
Then, after making its sheets split, with the liquids of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> and sour substances,

children.text: bhāvayed aṣṭayāmaṃ tu hyevaṃ śudhyati cābhrakam ||
children.translated_text: one should steep it for eight watches; in this way <s>abhraka</s> is purified.
After tying <s>abhraka</s> mixed with one-fourth part rice in a blanket,
one should keep it in water for three nights; when it is soaked, one should rub it with the hands.

children.text: kambalād galitaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vālukāsadṛśaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever fine material, like sand, has passed through the blanket,
that is called <s>dhānyābhraka</s>; next comes the accomplishment of its calcination.
Having made that <s>dhānyābhraka</s>, and having dried it, one should then triturate it
for a day in a mortar with the milks of <s>arka</s>, and make it into the shape of discs.
One should wrap it with leaves of <s>arka</s> and cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: punarmardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground again and cooked again, seven times repeatedly.
Then, in the same way, three firings should be given with decoctions of the aerial roots of the banyan.
It is calcined; there is no doubt here. One should apply it in all diseases.
Equal ghee with dead <s>abhraka</s> should be cooked in an iron vessel.

children.text: ghṛte jīrṇe tadabhraṃ tu sarvarogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: When the ghee has been digested, that <s>abhraka</s> should be used in all diseases.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s>, with the milks of <s>ravi</s> or with the liquid of <s>ravi</s> root,
being ground again and again and fired by cooking seven times, becomes calcined <s>abhraka</s>.

children.text: dhānyābhraṃ meghanādaiḥ kadalighanajalaiṣṭaṅkaṇāṅkolatoyaiḥ khalve saṃmardya gāḍhaṃ tadanu gajapuṭāndvādaśaivaṃ pradadyāt
children.translated_text: Having strongly triturated <s>dhānyābhra</s> in a mortar with meghanāda, the thick water of plantain, ṭaṅkaṇa, and water of aṅkola, one should then give twelve <s>gajapuṭa</s> firings in this way.

children.text: mīnākṣībhṛṅgatoyaistriphalajalayutairmardayetsaptavāraṃ gandhaṃ tulyaṃ ca dattvā pravaragajapuṭātpañcatāṃ yāti meghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should triturate it seven times with the waters of mīnākṣī and bhṛṅga, joined with triphalā-water; after adding sulphur equal in quantity, through an excellent <s>gajapuṭa</s>, <s>megha</s> comes to destruction, that is, calcination.
The three milks, water of <s>kumārī</s>, elephant urine, and human urine
Abhra, thoroughly triturated with vaṭabhṛṅga and goat's blood, together with these substances,
when subjected to puṭa-heating a hundred times, becomes a bhasma like a ruby.
Having taken dhānyābhraka, one should give three puṭas with decoctions of mustā,
and in the same way with waters of punarnavā and with juices of kāsamarda.
With leaves of nāgavallī, with ghee, and with milk, it should be given separately, one by one;
day by day, after triturating it with decoctions produced from the aerial roots of vaṭa,
afterwards one should give three puṭas, and then three puṭas with liquids of musalī,
three times with decoction of gokṣura, and three times one should puṭa it with juices of vānarī.
It should be cooked with juices of the bulb of mocā, and three times with those of kokilākṣa;
then one should puṭa it with juices, and then give one gentle puṭa with cow's milk.

children.text: dadhnā ghṛtena madhunā svacchayā sitayā tathā
children.translated_text: With curd, ghee, honey, clear sugar, and likewise white sugar,
one should give one puṭa with each; in this way the killing of abhra takes place.

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ dvau bhāgau ṭaṅkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: One part of dhānyābhraka and two parts of ṭaṅkaṇa,
having ground them, sealed them in a blind crucible, one should cook them with an intense fire.
When naturally cooled, the powder should be applied in all diseases.
One should use that which is free from moon-like glitter as a rasāyana in a purified body;
that which still has glitter should be known as poison, causing death like a tiger's hair.
Excellent water, cow's ghee, and abhra, with kalā and ṣaḍdika in equal parts,
should be cooked over a gentle fire as a linctus; this indeed produces amṛtīkaraṇa.

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍuruggrahaṇikāśūlāmakoṣṭhāmayān
children.translated_text: Divine abhra, accompanied by vellā and vyoṣa, joined with ghee, and taken in a valla measure, conquers wasting, anemia, grahaṇī disorder, colic, āma and abdominal diseases,

children.text: ārtiśvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharam mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ vijayate khaṃ hanti sarvāmayān ||
children.translated_text: pain, dyspnea, urinary disease, anorexia, difficult cough disease, weak digestive fire, and abdominal pain; kha destroys all diseases.

children.text: gaurītejaḥ paramamamṛtaṃ vātapittakṣayaghnaṃ prajñābodhi praśamitajaraṃ vṛṣyamāyuṣyamagryam
children.translated_text: The supreme nectar, the fire of Gaurī, destroys vāta, pitta, and wasting; it awakens intelligence, quiets old age, is aphrodisiac and foremost for longevity.

children.text: balyaṃ snigdhaṃ rucidamakaphaṃ dīpanaṃ śītavīryaṃ tattadyogaiḥ sakalagadahṛdvyoma sūtendrabandhi ||
children.translated_text: It strengthens, is unctuous, gives appetite, is not kapha-producing, kindles digestion, and has cooling potency; in each formulation vyoma removes every disease and binds mercury.
Alkaline and sour things, vidala, kola, karkaṭā, and kāravellaka,

children.text: vṛntākaṃ ca karīraṃ ca tailaṃ cābhre vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: as well as eggplant, karīra, and oil should be avoided when using abhra.

children.text: abhrakaṃ ca niśāyuktaṃ pippalī madhunā saha
children.translated_text: Abhraka together with niśā, pippalī, and honey
destroys the twenty kinds of prameha; there is no doubt about this.
Abhraka joined with gold destroys wasting disease;
silver, gold, and abhraka together are supreme for increasing the bodily tissues.

children.text: abhrakaṃ ca harītakyā guḍena saha yojitam
children.translated_text: Abhraka used with harītakī and jaggery,
joined with elā and sugar, destroys raktapitta.
Trikaṭu, triphalā, cāturjāta, and sugar,
should be licked with honey in the morning; it destroys wasting, piles, and anemia.
Mixed with guḍūcī-sattva and khaṇḍa sugar, it destroys urinary disease;
mixed with elā, gokṣura, bhūdhātrī, sugar, and a cow product,
when regularly used in the morning, it prevents urinary disease and dysuria.
Joined with pippalī and honey, it removes dizziness and chronic fever.
Joined with honey and triphalā, it is considered to nourish the eyesight;
vyoma joined with mūrvā-sattva also destroys wounds.
With cow's milk and kṣīrakanda it is supreme for increasing strength;
vyoma joined with bhallātaka prevents the disorder of piles.

children.text: nāgaraṃ pauṣkaraṃ bhārgī gaganaṃ madhunā saha
children.translated_text: Nāgara, pauṣkara, bhārgī, and gagana with honey,
eaten with aśvagandhā, prevent diseases of vāta.
Cāturjāta, sugar, and abhra prevent pitta disease;
kaṭphala, pippalī, and honey prevent diseases of śleṣman.
Abhra joined with all alkalis is supreme for increasing digestive fire;
it destroys urinary retention, dysuria, and even urinary stones.
Joined with the juice of vijayā, it is supreme for restraining semen;
joined with clove and honey, it is supreme for increasing the bodily tissues.
Cow's milk together with sugar destroys pitta disease;
abhraka, prepared according to rule and used with an appropriate regimen,
destroys wrinkles and grey hair, and one lives for a hundred autumns.

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍusaṃgrahaṇikāśūlaṃ ca kuṣṭhāmayam
children.translated_text: Divine abhra, accompanied by vellā and vyoṣa, joined with ghee, and taken in a valla measure, removes wasting, anemia, grahaṇī disorder, colic, and skin disease,

children.text: sarvaśvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharaṃ mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ pariharecchleṣmāmayān niścitam ||
children.translated_text: all dyspneic disorders, prameha, anorexia, difficult cough disease, weak digestive fire, abdominal pain, and certainly diseases of śleṣman.
There is nothing superior to this for destroying old age and death.
Golden in color, heavy, unctuous, and having a slight bluish sheen,
and rubbed on the touchstone like gold: that is the best hemamākṣika.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ mākṣikaṃ kuryādāndhyaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣayaṃ krimīn
children.translated_text: Unpurified mākṣika causes blindness, skin disease, wasting, and worms;
therefore kanakamākṣika should be purified with care.
Three parts of mākṣika should be taken, with one fourth part of saindhava;
one should cook it with juice of jambīra, or with liquid of bījapūra.

children.text: gharṣitaṃ lohapātre ca yāti pātraṃ ca raktatām
children.translated_text: When rubbed in an iron vessel, the vessel becomes red;
then such svarṇamākṣika attains purity.
Mākṣika is purified when cooked with castor oil and citron water;
or, purified with water from the banana bulb for two ghaṭikās,
heated and thrown into decoction of varā, mākṣika attains purity.
With exudations from agasti leaves, śigru root is well ground;
placed in that, puṭa-heated, and cooked with the acid of nimbūja, it becomes purified.
Having added sulphur in the amount of one fourth of the mākṣika, one should triturate it.
Then a good pellet should be made with the oil of <s>urubūka</s>.
Having placed it in a covered earthen saucer, one should heat it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (large furnace-pit heating).
After putting the husk of grain above and below, one should take it out when it has cooled.
The <s>bhasma</s> (calx) of <s>mākṣika</s> becomes like vermilion; there is no doubt.
In goat's urine, or in oil, or in a decoction made from <s>kulattha</s>,

children.text: takre vā gharṣitaṃ pakvaṃ mriyate svarṇamākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: or in buttermilk, when it is rubbed and cooked, <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> is killed, that is, incinerated.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is bitter and sweet; it destroys urinary disease, hemorrhoids, wasting, and skin disease.
It removes kapha and pitta, is cooling, a <s>yogavāhin</s> (vehicle enhancing compounds), and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
<s>Mākṣika</s>, having the luster of silver and gold and being purified, gives great benefit when well used.
It removes urinary disease, skin disease, worms, swelling, anemia, fever, and epilepsy, and it conquers urinary stone.
Uncooked <s>mākṣika</s> ore, though heavy, produces weak digestion, severe loss of strength, constipation, and other bad diseases,
and also dirt and ulceration preceded by sores.

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> ore destroys all diseases, is truly the life of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), and is supremely aphrodisiac.
It joins the two metals that are hard to combine, is superior in qualities, and is foremost among all <s>rasāyana</s>s.
<s>Tāramākṣika</s> is like bronze; when rubbed on a touchstone it is like silver.
That which is heavy, unctuous, and white should be the best <s>tāramākṣika</s>.
The defects in <s>tāramākṣika</s> should be known as the same as in <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>.
Therefore its purification is described as follows, for the pacification of those defects.
For one day, in the sun, a <s>bhāvanā</s> (levigation/impregnation) should be given with the juices of <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>jambīra</s>.

children.text: ātape bhāvanā deyā śuddhaṃ syāt tāramākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāramākṣika</s> thereby becomes purified.
The incineration of <s>tāramākṣika</s> should be understood as like that of <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>.
The qualities of <s>vimalā</s> are somewhat less than those of <s>kanakamākṣika</s>.
Unpurified <s>tāla</s> takes away life and produces kapha, vāta, and urinary disease.
It causes heat, boils, and contraction of the limbs; therefore one should purify it.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā taccūrṇaṃ kāñjike kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having broken <s>tālaka</s> into particles, one should throw that powder into sour gruel.
Cooked for one <s>yāma</s> in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), <s>tālaka</s> is purified.

children.text: sadalaṃ tālakaṃ śuddhaṃ punarnavyā rasena tu
children.translated_text: Pure <s>tālaka</s> with its flakes should again be triturated in a mortar for one day
with the juice of <s>punarnavā</s>; afterwards it should be dried.
After drying it, one should make a ball of it, and dry that too.
Then one should fill half a pot with the alkalis of <s>punarnavā</s>.
Placing that ball there, one should fill it again with the same substance.

children.text: ā kaṇṭhaṃ piṭharaṃ tasya pidhānaṃ dhārayenmukhe ||
children.translated_text: Up to the neck of the vessel, one should place a lid on its mouth.
Having set the pot on the hearth, one should gradually increase the fire.
For five uninterrupted days one should keep the fire burning.

children.text: evaṃ tu mriyate tālaṃ mātrā tasyaikaraktikā
children.translated_text: In this way <s>tāla</s> is incinerated; its dose is one <s>raktikā</s>.
Various accompanying vehicles should be used as appropriate.
<s>Haritāla</s> is pungent, unctuous, astringent, and hot, and it removes poison,
itch, diseases called skin disease, blood disorders, vāta, pitta, kapha, and wounds.
<s>Tālaka</s> removes diseases and skin disease, and wards off death and old age.

children.text: śodhitaṃ kurute vīryaṃ kāṃtiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When purified, it produces vigor, beauty, growth, and longevity.

children.text: manaḥśilā mandabalaṃ karoti jantuṃ dhruvaṃ śodhanam antareṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s>, without purification, certainly makes a creature weak in strength.

children.text: malasya bandhaṃ kila mūtrarogaṃ saśarkaraṃ kṛcchragadaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: It indeed causes obstruction of feces, urinary disease with gravel, and painful urinary disorder.
One should cook <s>manaḥśilā</s> for three days in goat's urine in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
One should impregnate it seven times with goat's urine; it attains purification.
Impregnated seven times with water from <s>agasti</s> leaves,
or with ginger juice, <s>manaḥśilā</s> is purified.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is heavy, complexion-promoting, fluid, hot, scraping, and pungent.
It is bitter and unctuous, and removes poison, dyspnea, cough, possession, poisoning, and blood disorders.
<s>Srotoñjana</s> is said to be twofold, according to the distinction of white and black appearance.
Both kinds, steamed with water of <s>triphalā</s>, attain purification.
<s>Sauvīra</s> is constipating, sweet, beneficial for the eyes, and conquers kapha and pitta.
It removes hiccup, wasting, and blood disorders, is cooling, and <s>srotoñjana</s> also is like this.
One should rub <s>tuttha</s> with the excrement of a cat and of a pigeon.
After adding one tenth part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, one should cook it in a light <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: puṭaṃ dadhnā puṭaṃ kṣaudrairdeyaṃ tutthaṃ viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: A <s>puṭa</s> should be given with curds and a <s>puṭa</s> with honey; <s>tuttha</s> is purified.
With an equal quantity of the uncertain substance read as <s>otorviśā</s>, <s>tuttha</s> should be mixed with honey and with a quarter part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
Thus, heated three times in <s>puṭa</s>s, it is purified and free from vomiting and dizziness.

children.text: tutthakaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ viśadaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Tutthaka</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, clear, and light.
It is scraping, purgative, beneficial for the eyes, and removes itch, worms, and poison.
It destroys kapha, blood disorders, pitta, and skin disease, and eliminates urinary disease and fat.

children.text: nṛmūtre vātha gomūtre saptāhaṃ rasakaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: One should cook <s>rasaka</s> for seven days in human urine or cow urine,
by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>; it becomes purified, and then one should employ it in operations.

children.text: kharparaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ vāmakaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Kharpara</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, emetic, and light.
It is scraping, breaking, cooling, beneficial for the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It is considered supreme for destroying poison, blood disorders, skin disease, and itch.

children.text: raso vipraḥ sito raktaḥ kṣatriyaḥ pīta ūrujaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury is fourfold by distinction of color: the white is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the red a <s>kṣatriya</s>, the yellow a <s>vaiśya</s>,
and the black is said to be a <s>śūdra</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kalpyate kalpe guṭikāyāṃ ca bāhujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is prescribed in transformative rites, and the arm-born, the <s>kṣatriya</s>, in pills.
Likewise the <s>vaiśya</s> is used in metallurgical operations, and the <s>śūdra</s> in other work.
That which is very blue within, bright-limbed without, and shining like the midday moon

children.text: śasto'tha dhūmraḥ paripāṇḍuraśca citro na yojyo rasakarmasiddhyai ||
children.translated_text: is praised; but smoky, very pale, and variegated mercury should not be used for success in mercury operations.

children.text: pūrvair doṣā rasendrasya ye ca proktā manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The defects of <s>rasendra</s> that were previously stated by the wise
Now, for the pacification of these, the procedure is being stated.
Mala, śikhin, and viṣa are the three natural faults of mercury.

children.text: mūrchāṃ malena kurute śikhinā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: By mala it causes fainting; by śikhin, burning; and by viṣa, death.

children.text: malena mūrchāṃ dahanena dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ vitanoti sūtaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury brings about fainting through mala, burning through fire, and death through poison.
Here I shall describe the purification of this threefold natural fault beginning with mala.

children.text: nāgo vaṅgo malo vahniścāñcalyaṃ ca girirviṣam
children.translated_text: Nāga, vaṅga, mala, vahni, fickleness, giri, and viṣa:

children.text: pārade kañcukā sapta guṇā naisargikā ime ||
children.translated_text: these are said to be the seven natural coverings of mercury.
With powders of red brick, niśā, soot, sāra, spider-web, and ash,
mixed with the juice of jambīra, one acts for the removal of the nāga fault.
With the dust of the roots of viśālā and aṅkola, and with kāñjika,
slowly and gradually, by one's own hand, one frees it from the vaṅga fault.
Kanyā, together with powder produced from the root of rājavṛkṣa,
serves for removing the mala fault; citraka removes the fault of vahni.
Black dhattūra destroys fickleness; the three pungents destroy giri.
Triphalā is for the destruction of poison; kanyā removes the seven coverings.

children.text: āragvadho hanti malaṃ prayatnāt kumārikā sapta hi kañcukāṃśca
children.translated_text: Āragvadha carefully destroys mala, and kumārikā indeed destroys the seven coverings.

children.text: aṅkolamūlaṃ ca viṣaṃ nihanyādrasasya vahniḥ kila pāvakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The root of aṅkola destroys the poison of mercury, and vahni, they say, also destroys pāvaka.

children.text: pratyekaṃ saptavāraṃ ca marditaḥ pārado bhavet
children.translated_text: Mercury should be triturated seven times with each one separately.
Then it attains complete purity and becomes fit for all preparations.
Kumārī, triphalā, vyoṣa, citraka, and the juice of naimbuka:

children.text: dinaikaṃ marditaṃ kṛtvā śuddho bhavati pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when mercury is triturated with these for one day, it becomes purified.
After each trituration one should wash it with warm āranāla.

children.text: rasaṃ tatra prayātaṃ tu śoṣayitvātha pātayet ||
children.translated_text: The mercury that has gone into it should then be dried and subjected to distillation.

children.text: gṛhītvā prakṣipet sūtaṃ syādevaṃ pāradaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Having taken it, one should put in the sūta; in this way mercury becomes clean.
The physician should mix in everything in the amount of one-sixteenth of the mercury.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ pradeyaṃ ca palaṃ mardane taptakhalvake
children.translated_text: A pala of powder should be supplied for trituration in a heated mortar.
Having dug the ground, one should place there a fire of goat-dung husks.
The mortar set above it is called a heated mortar by the learned.
This trituration has been taught by the learned for the thorough purification of kha.
Tryūṣaṇa, triphalā, vandhyākanda, and the two kṣudrās,
together with citraka, niśākṣāra, kanyā, arka, and kanaka liquids:

children.text: sūtaṃ kṛtena kvāthena vārān sapta vimardayet
children.translated_text: with the decoction made from these one should triturate sūta seven times.

children.text: itthaṃ sa mūrchitaḥ sūto jahyātsaptāpi kañcukān ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when stupefied, that sūta casts off all seven coverings.
Thereafter one should raise up the sūta in the sun, moistened with nimbuka.
The special raising-up is in a powder-distillation apparatus.
Having set it on the fire up to the upper vessel, one should collect the clean mercury.
One should bind the mercury in fourfold cloth in a saucer containing garlic,

children.text: niyantrya dolāyantre tu prakalpya divasaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: arrange it in a dolā apparatus, and cook it for a day.
In husk-water with a paste of vyoṣa, triphalā, vahni, and kanyā,
this steaming is prescribed for the removal of the remaining faults.
For sūta less than a pala, or more than a hundred palas,
the saṃskāra should not be performed; another saṃskāra is required in that case.
The beginning of mercury purification should be undertaken on an auspicious day.

children.text: ekānte dhāmani śubhe purābhyarcyo hi bhairavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a good, secluded dwelling, <s>Bhairava</s> should first be worshipped.

children.text: sūto'śuddhatayā guṇaṃ na kurute kuṣṭhāgnimāndyakrimīñchardyarocakajāḍyadāhamaraṇaṃ dhatte nṛṇāṃ sevanāt
children.translated_text: Because of impurity, sūta does not produce its virtue; when consumed by men it causes skin disease, weak digestion, worms, vomiting, anorexia, dullness, burning, and death.

children.text: śuddhaḥ syātsakalāmayaughaśamano yo yogavāho mṛto yuktyā ṣaḍguṇagandhayuggadaharo yogena dhātvādibhuk ||
children.translated_text: When purified, properly killed, and joined with six parts of sulphur, it becomes a carrier of preparations, pacifies the whole mass of diseases, removes disease, and consumes bodily constituents and the like in due combination.

children.text: mūrcchārto gadahṛttathaiva khagatiṃ datte nibaddho 'rthadas tadbhasmāmayavārddhakādiharaṇaṃ dṛkpuṣṭikāntipradam
children.translated_text: When stupefied it removes disease; when bound it grants sky-going; that ash removes disease, old age, and the like, and gives sight, nourishment, and beauty.

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ mṛtyuvināśanaṃ balakaraṃ kāntājanānandadaṃ śārdūlātulasattvakṛt kramabhujāṃ yogānusāri sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: It is aphrodisiac, destroys death, gives strength, delights women, produces a power unequalled by a tiger, and clearly follows the successive preparations.

children.text: mūrchāṃ gato yo harate ca rogānbaddho yadā khecaratāmupaiti
children.translated_text: When it has entered stupefaction it removes diseases, and when bound it attains the state of moving in the sky.
When dissolved, it becomes the giver of every prosperity; this lord of mercury shines exceedingly.

children.text: mūrchitvā harati rujaṃ bandhanamanubhūya muktido bhavati
children.translated_text: Having been stupefied, it removes pain; after undergoing binding, it becomes a giver of liberation.

children.text: amarīkaroti hi mṛtaṃ ko'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt ||
children.translated_text: Even when dead it makes one immortal; what other benefactor is there than sūta?

children.text: arthāḥ sahāyā nikhilaṃ ca śāstraṃ hastakriyā karmaṇi kauśalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Materials, assistants, the whole science, manual practice, and skill in the operation,
constant effort, devotion to the task, and fire: through these qualities the lordly sūta is perfected.
Alternatively, mercury extracted from darada, steamed in a dolā containing salt water,
should be taken, and with it a medicinal preparation may be made as desired.
Darada, firmly ground for a watch of the day with nimbū juice,
should be collected as stainless mercury by means of an upward-distillation apparatus.
Alternatively, mercury should be triturated with bindulī insects for three days.
With salts and sour substances its mouth becomes capable of consuming metals.

children.text: sāsyo rasaḥ syātpaṭuśigrututthaiḥ sarājikaiḥ śoṣaṇakais trirātram
children.translated_text: Mercury with such a mouth, with paṭu, śigru products, and mustard, and with drying agents, for three nights,
being ground and then made thin by steaming, eats gold and the other chief metals, indeed all metals.
Having placed mercury in a heated mortar, with husk-fires beneath the hearth,

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣipedgandhamevaṃ vai ṣaḍguṇaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: one should add sulphur little by little; thus one should proceed up to six times the quantity.
One should place water in an earthen pot, and in its middle a saucer,
resembling the lid of a large pot and furnished with a girdle in the middle.
Having placed excellent purified mercury in the middle of the girdle...
Upon the mercury one should place an equal portion of sulphur powder.
After placing a saucer over it, one should apply a sealing of ash and clay.
Over that one should give a heating with four cow-dung cakes.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punargandhaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ jīryate budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, again and again, the wise digest sulphur into it up to six times its amount.
When the sulphur has been digested, mercury becomes sharp in fire and effective in all operations.

children.text: same gandhe tu rogaghno dviguṇe rājayakṣmanut
children.translated_text: With an equal amount of sulphur it destroys diseases; with twice the amount it removes pulmonary consumption.
When sulphur three times its amount has been digested, it destroys the pride of passionate women.
With four times the amount it becomes brilliant and skilled in all sciences.
With five times the amount it becomes perfected; with six times the amount it destroys death.
One who gives fire to the king of mercury for one day

children.text: dravanti tasya pāpāni kurvannapi na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: has his sins melted away; even while acting, he is not tainted.

children.text: rambhā vīrā snuhī caiva kṣīrakañcukireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>snuhī</s>, and also <s>kṣīrakañcukī</s>,
as well as <s>dinārī</s>, <s>gorambhā</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s>:

children.text: ebhistu marditaḥ sūtaḥ punarjanma na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: mercury triturated with these has no rebirth.
When mercury is properly placed in the middle of a flowered, charming chamber,
it becomes bound within some days through the power of the flowers.
One should firmly triturate the root of <s>bhūlatāśīvarī</s> with water.
One should smear a crucible inside with that root and place mercury in its middle.
One should put that crucible, measuring five ṭaṅkas, on charcoal.

children.text: evaṃ baddho bhavetsūto mūṣāntaḥstho dṛḍho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In this way mercury becomes bound; remaining inside the crucible, it becomes firm.
Kept in the middle of the mouth, it destroys diseases of the mouth.
When mercury has circulated through the body, a man conquers old age and grey hair.
It arrests the mass of weapons and causes the arousal of desire.

children.text: punarnavaṃ vayaḥ kuryāt sādhakānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It makes youth new again for practitioners; there is no doubt.
One should prepare a pair of crucibles from the seeds of <s>apāmārga</s>.
In that joined container one should place mercury mixed with <s>malayū</s> milk.
Flowers of <s>droṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>arimedaka</s>
should be made into powder, placed below and above, and then sealed.
The wise man should seal that ball properly in a joined clay crucible.

children.text: mudrāṃ dattvā śoṣayitvā tato gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After sealing it and drying it, he should then cook it in a gajapuṭa.
By just one such heating, mercury ash is produced.
One should triturate purified mercury and an equal amount of sulphur with banyan latex.
One should cook it in an earthen vessel with banyan wood and triturate it.
Cooked for a day with a mild fire, it certainly becomes ash of mercury.

children.text: dviguñjaṃ parṇakhaṇḍena puṣṭim agniṃ ca vardhayet ||
children.translated_text: Two guñjās, taken with a piece of leaf, increase nourishment and digestive fire.
Two palas of purified mercury, half a pala of purified sulphur,
and half a karṣa of navasāra should be triturated with citron juice.
One should put it into a glass bottle and coat it seven times with clay and cloth.
Having smeared that glass bottle, one should dry it firmly in the sun.
Then one should place the bottle in a perforated vessel, in a sand apparatus.
One should fill the bottle up to the neck with the desired sand.
After worshipping five maidens, one should then place it on the hearth.

children.text: pacedyāmāṣṭakaṃ caiva kūpikāṃ ca kṣaṇe kṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: One should cook the bottle for eight yāmas and examine it moment by moment.
Having cooked it in the apparatus after cleaning it, one should remove it when self-cooled.
The substance, resembling darada, should be taken; it is hard for gods and demons to obtain.
One should use it for the destruction of diseases, with the appropriate vehicle for each disease.

children.text: vallaṃ vā vallayugmaṃ vā kaṇayā madhunā saha ||
children.translated_text: A valla, or two vallas, may be taken with kaṇā and honey.
When taken, it displays the pleasure of love to women who desire passion.
It quickly binds semen and destroys the intoxication of women.
This sindūra, born from the seed of <s>Hara</s>, removes dryness and weak digestion, and removes consumption beginning with yakṣmā, wasting, anemia, swelling, abdominal disease, gulma, and prameha.

children.text: śūlaplīhavināśanaṃ jvaraharaṃ duṣṭavraṇān nāśayed arśāṃsi grahaṇībhagandaraharaṃ charditridoṣāpaham ||
children.translated_text: It destroys colic and spleen disease, removes fever, destroys bad wounds, and removes piles, grahaṇī disease, fistula, vomiting, and the three doṣas.

children.text: sūtaḥ pañcapalaḥ svadoṣarahitastattulyabhāgo balir dvau caitau navasārapādakalitau saṃmardya kūpyāṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: Mercury, five palas, free from its faults, with an equal portion of sulphur, these two together with a quarter part of navasāra, are to be well triturated and placed in a bottle.

children.text: tāṃ yantre sikatākhyake talabile paktvārkayāmaṃ himaṃ bhittvā kuṅkumapiñjaraṃ rasavaraṃ bhasmādaded vaidyarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: Having cooked that in the apparatus called the sand apparatus, in the lower pit, for a solar day, and when cold having broken it, the king of physicians should take the excellent mercury ash, tawny like saffron.

children.text: vāte sakṣaudrapippalyapi ca kapharuji tryūṣaṇaṃ sāgnicūrṇaṃ pitte sailā sitā syād vraṇavati bṛhatīnāgarārdrāmṛtāmbu
children.translated_text: For vāta, its vehicle is honey and pippalī; in disease of kapha, tryūṣaṇa with digestive powder; for pitta, cardamom with sugar; for wounds, water of bṛhatī, nāgara, fresh ginger, and amṛtā.

children.text: puṣṭau sājyatriyāmā haranayanaphalā śālmalīpuṣpavṛntaṃ kiṃvā kāntālalāṭābharaṇarasapateḥ syād anupānametat ||
children.translated_text: For nourishment, it is taken with ghee, triyāmā, haranayana fruit, and stalks of śālmalī flowers; or this may be the vehicle for the lord of rasa that is the ornament on a beloved woman's forehead.

children.text: bhāgo rasasya traya eva bhāgā gandhasya māṣaḥ pavanāśanasya
children.translated_text: One part mercury, three parts sulphur, and one māṣa of pavanāśana:

children.text: saṃmardya gāḍhaṃ sakalaṃ subhāṇḍe tāṃ kajjalīṃ kācakṛte nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: having triturated all of it thoroughly in a good vessel, one should place that kajjalī in a glass vessel.

children.text: saṃrudhya mṛtkarpaṭakairvaṭīnāṃ mukhe sacūrṇāṃ guṭikāṃ ca dattvā
children.translated_text: After sealing it with clay and cloth, and placing a powdered pill at the mouth of the pellets,

children.text: kramāgninā trīṇi dināni paktvā tāṃ vālukāyantragatāṃ tataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: one should cook it for three days with gradual fire, with it set in the sand apparatus; then it will be ready.
The ash of the lord's substance, red like a bandhūka flower, should be administered in diseases.

children.text: nijānupānairmaraṇaṃ jarāṃ ca hantyasya vallaḥ kramasevanena ||
children.translated_text: Through gradual use, one valla of it, with its proper vehicles, destroys death and old age.

children.text: apaharati rogavṛndaṃ draḍhayati kāyaṃ mahadbalaṃ kurute
children.translated_text: It removes the multitude of diseases, strengthens the body, and produces great strength.

children.text: śukraśatāni ca sūte sindūrākhyo rasaḥ puṃsām ||
children.translated_text: The rasa called sindūra produces hundreds of measures of semen in men.
Mercury ash is especially capable of consuming every wasting disease and removes wounds, skin disease, fistula, and urinary disorders.
It increases strength, radiance, and semen, and removes all diseases.

children.text: palamātraṃ rasaṃ śuddhaṃ tāvanmātraṃ tu gandhakam
children.translated_text: One pala-measure of pure mercury, and just the same measure of sulfur,
having made them properly into kajjalī with the water of banyan shoots,
after giving three impregnations, one should place it in the middle of an earthen dish.
Having made a tortoise-shaped apparatus, one should fill it with sand.
Then the physician should apply a gentle fire for four yāmas.
Rasasindūra is produced, resembling the young red sun.
By distinction of the accompanying vehicle, it produces various effects.
It destroys consumption, skin disease, vāta, spleen disease, and urinary disease, and removes pallor.
Just as oil placed in water spreads at that very moment,
so this medicine spreads through the limbs by means of its anupāna.

children.text: pippalī madhunā sārdhaṃ vātamehaṃ hinasti ca
children.translated_text: Pippalī together with honey destroys vātic urinary disease.
Triphalā together with sugar is remembered as removing pittic urinary disease.

children.text: pippalī maricaṃ śuṇṭhī bhārgī ca madhunā saha
children.translated_text: Pippalī, pepper, dry ginger, and bhārgī, together with honey,
pacify cough and dyspnea and destroy colic.
Turmeric together with sugar removes disorders of the blood.
The three pungents, triphalā, and vāsā remove jaundice, pallor, and weak digestion.

children.text: pippalī citrakaṃ pathyā tathā sauvarcalaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: One should add pippalī, citraka, pathyā, and likewise sauvarcala salt.
It is supreme for destroying weak digestion, constipation, and pain in the heart.
With śilājatu, also cardamom, and sugar-candy,
this is praised in dysuria; it is true, as stated by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
Clove, saffron, patrī, hiṅgula, karahāṭikā,
pippalī, and vijayā: these should be made equal in measure.
One should add half-parts of camphor, ahiphena, and nāga.
Having ground everything together, one should administer it for increase of dhātu.
Sauvarcala salt, clove, bhūnimba, and harītakī:
by the use of this as an anupāna, it destroys every fever.
Likewise it is said to be purgative when used with sauvarcala and the three fruits.

children.text: lavaṅgaṃ kuṅkumaṃ caiva daradena ca saṃyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Clove and saffron, combined with darada,
should be eaten together with betel; it is excellent for increasing dhātu.
With the application of vidārī powder it is considered to increase dhātu.
Combined with vijayā and dīpya, it removes disorders arising from vomiting.
Sauvarcala salt, turmeric, vijayā, and dīpyaka:
with this one should immediately destroy abdominal pain that has just arisen.
Four vallas of palāśa seed, and twice as much jaggery:
by the use of this as an anupāna, it destroys worm disorder.

children.text: ahiphenaṃ lavaṅgaṃ ca daradaṃ vijayā tathā
children.translated_text: Ahiphena, clove, darada, and likewise vijayā:
through this anupāna it immediately destroys every diarrhea.
With sauvarcala and dīpya it is excellent for removing weak digestion.
It also produces appetite; this was stated by Siddhanāgeśvara.
With the use of guḍūcī-sattva it is remembered as promoting all nourishment.
Joined with suitable anupānas, it destroys all diseases.
Rock salt, amṛtā, coriander, cumin, and fresh ginger,
taṇḍulīyaka, eggplant, paṭola, and parched grain preparations,
wheat, old śāli rice, cow's milk, ghee, and curds,

children.text: haṃsodakaṃ mudgarasaṃ rasendre ca hitaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: haṃsodaka water and mung-bean soup: these are known as beneficial with rasendra.
Oil massage should be applied when there is impurity, with Nārāyaṇa oil and the like.
A weak person should be sprinkled on the head with cold water.
When there is thirst, he should take coconut water and mung soup with sugar.
He should eat the fruits of grapes, pomegranate, dates, and plantain.
Bṛhatī, bilva, pumpkin, bamboo shoots, bitter gourd,
black gram, lentils, niṣpāva beans, horse gram, salt, and sesame,
fasting, rubbing with powders, bathing, copper vessels, liquor and wine,
marshy meat, sour grain gruel, and eating on a plantain leaf,

children.text: kāṃsyake guru viṣṭambhi tīkṣṇaṃ coṣṇaṃ bhṛśaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: bronze vessels, and what is heavy, obstructive, sharp, and very hot:
these were formerly declared by the great seers to be unsuitable for sūtarāja.
Pumpkin, cucumber, jujube, watermelon, and karamardaka,
and karīra and the like, in groups beginning with these six, should be avoided by one taking rasa.

children.text: caturdhā gandhakaḥ prokto raktaḥ pītaḥ sito'sitaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulfur is said to be fourfold: red, yellow, white, and black.
The red is recommended for gold operations, and the yellow for rasāyana.
The white is best for application to wounds and the like, while the black is very hard to obtain.
This sulfur, placed in a cloth over a vessel of milk, becomes purified by a kūrma-puṭa.
With the kajjalī made from these two, mercury and sulfur, together with anupānas, it destroys all diseases.
Sulfur is pungent and bitter; its potency is hot, and it is astringent and flowing.
It is bilious and pungent in post-digestive effect, and conquers itching, erysipelas, and parasites.
It destroys skin disease, consumption, spleen disease, phlegm, and vāta; it is a rasāyana.
This sulfur, when unpurified, causes skin disease and burning.
It causes loss of semen and vitality, weakness, and destroys taste.
Darada is said to be of three kinds: carmāra, śukatuṇḍaka,
and haṃsapāda as the third; each later one is more excellent in qualities.
Carmāra should be very red; śukāsyaka is somewhat yellow.
That which has white lines and is coral-like is called haṃsapāda.

children.text: aśuddho daradaḥ kuryād āndhyaṃ kṣaiṇyaṃ klamaṃ bhramam
children.translated_text: Unpurified darada causes blindness, wasting, fatigue, dizziness,

children.text: mohaṃ mehaṃ ca saṃśodhyaḥ kramādvaidyaistu hiṅgulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bewilderment, and urinary disease; therefore hiṅgula should be purified in due order by physicians.
Darada, impregnated with ewe's milk and with the sour group
seven times with care, certainly attains purification.
Then one should place a valla-measure of tāla paste in a shallow dish.
In that, a fragment of darada equal to a karṣa should be put.
The wise man should fill it there with twice as much fresh ginger juice.
Then he should place flowers, each of the measure of a māṣa, all around.
Having covered it with a pair of earthen saucers, he should cook it on a stove over a medium fire
for the duration of three ghaṭikās; then, having taken it down, he should grind it.

children.text: tāmbūle guñjamātraṃ tu deyaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ matam
children.translated_text: A guñjā-measure should be given in betel leaf; it is regarded as nourishing.

children.text: pāṇḍau kṣaye ca śūle ca sarvarogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be applied in pāṇḍu, wasting disease, colic, and in all diseases.
Diamond placed in the tuber of vyāghrī should be cooked in a dolā apparatus
for seven days with decoctions of kodrava; the thunderbolt-stone becomes pure.
Taking the root of a three-year-old cotton plant, he should grind it,
or he should grind it thoroughly with the own juices of a three-year-old nāgavallī.
He should place the diamond in that pellet, seal it, and cook it in a gajapuṭa.
In this way, with seven puṭas, the thunderbolt-stone surely reaches calcination.
Heated twenty-one times and sprinkled with donkey urine,
one should grind tālaka with bedbugs and place the thunderbolt-stone in that pellet.
Blown in the fire and sprinkled with horse urine, according to the previous procedure,
that diamond becomes ash, beautiful like a conch and the moon.
One should put the repeatedly heated diamond into a horse-gram decoction combined with hiṅgu and rock salt;
after being heated again and again, twenty-one times, it becomes powder.

children.text: maṇḍūkaṃ kāṃsyaje pātre nigṛhya sthāpayet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The prudent man should confine a frog in a bronze vessel and keep it there.
Frightened, it will urinate there; into that urine he should throw the diamond.

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ ca bahudhā vajrasyaivaṃ mṛtirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: Heated again and again many times, in this way the diamond is calcined.

children.text: vajraṃ samīrakaphapittagadān nihanti vajropamaṃ ca kurute vapur uttamaśri
children.translated_text: Diamond destroys diseases of vāta, kapha, and pitta, and makes the body diamond-like and of excellent splendor.
It removes consumption, wasting, dizziness, fistula, urinary disease, fatness, pāṇḍu, abdominal disease, swelling, and impotence or sterility.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajravacchodhyaṃ nīlaṃ vā lohitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Vaikrānta, like diamond, should be purified, whether blue or red.
It should be sprinkled with horse urine while repeatedly heated, fourteen times.
Then one should place it in a pellet made from the five parts of the sheep-dugdhī plant;
having sealed it in a crucible-puṭa, he should roast it, and should do this seven times.
Vaikrānta becomes ash and should be used in place of diamond.
It destroys vāta, pitta, and wind, has the six tastes, and makes the body firm.
It removes pāṇḍu, abdominal disease, fever, dyspnea, cough, consumption, and urinary disease.
Ruby is purified by sour liquid, pearl by jayantī,
coral by the group of alkalis, and emerald by cow milk.
Topaz is purified by combination with horse-gram decoction,
gomeda by rocanā substances, and cat’s-eye by triphalā water.

children.text: nīlaṃ nīlīrasair vajraṃ vinā śudhyati dolayā ||
children.translated_text: Sapphire is purified by juices of nīlī; except for diamond, it is purified in a dolā.
One should steam gems, pearls, and corals in a dolikā apparatus
with the fresh juice of jayantī for one yāma; that is their purification.
With śilā, tālaka, and sulphur ground together with lakuca juice,
all gems other than diamond are indeed calcined by eight puṭas.
One should sprinkle pearls, corals, and all gems, each separately seven times,
after heating them fully again and again, with kumārī, taṇḍulīya, and breast milk.
Pearls, corals, and likewise all gems,
of various colors, are calcined in a moment; there is no doubt here.
Pearls and corals should be killed as stated for mākṣika.
All gems should be purified and calcined like diamond.
Gems and secondary gems are beneficial to the eyes, mobile,
cooling, astringent, sweet, and auspicious.
They are aphrodisiac, auspicious, and productive of life, satisfaction, and nourishment.
They dispel planets, misfortune, poison, wasting, sin, and distress.
They destroy consumption, pāṇḍu, urinary disease, piles, cough, dyspnea, and fistula,
as well as fever, erysipelas, skin disease, colic, dysuria, wounds, and disorders;

children.text: ghnanti puṣṭiṃ yaśaḥ kāntiṃ puṇyāni ca nṛṇāṃ bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and they greatly produce nourishment, fame, beauty, and merit for men.
In summer, mountains, heated by the sun,
exude the essence of their minerals like resin; that is called śilājatu.
Then, in the hot season, when the sun is blazing, with a cloudless sky and no wind, on a level place,
one should set four black-iron vessels in the sun, giving the matter careful attention.

children.text: śilājatu śreṣṭhamavāpya pātre prakṣipya toyaṃ dviguṇaṃ tato'smāt
children.translated_text: Having obtained excellent śilājatu, he should put it in a vessel and add twice as much water to it.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ tadardhaṃ śṛtamatra dattvā viśodhayettanmṛditaṃ yathāvat ||
children.translated_text: Having poured in hot water boiled down by half, he should purify that substance there after properly crushing it.
Then whatever black substance rises upward, like a film, through contact with the sun rays,
he should place that from the vessel into another; within it he should put hot water.

children.text: tataśca tasmādaparatra pātre tasmācca pātrādaparatra bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then from that into another vessel, and again from that vessel into another,
again placing elsewhere the black substance that has been collected, he should take it back once more.
When the water above is pure and clear, and, through its clarified condition, the impurity has gone below,

children.text: tadā tyajettatsalilaṃ malaṃ ca śilājatu syājjalaśuddhamevam ||
children.translated_text: then he should discard that water and the impurity; śilājatu is thus purified by water.

children.text: vahnau kṣiptaṃ tu nirdhūmaṃ yattu liṅgopamaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When thrown into fire it should be smokeless and resemble a liṅga.
When thrown into water on the tip of a blade of grass, it sinks downward like a thread.
If it has the smell of cow urine and is impure-looking, it should be known as purified śilājatu.
Śilājatu is a rasāyana; it is pungent, bitter, hot, and removes worms, wasting, abdominal disease, splitting pain, stone, swelling, pāṇḍu, and itching.
It conquers urinary disease, vomiting, and skin disease, removes kapha, vāta, and piles, and drives away wrinkles, grey hair, mental disorders, cough, and dysuria.
When impure, it causes burning, fainting, dizziness, disorders of pitta and blood, and wasting.
Śilājatu produces dullness of the digestive fire and obstruction of stool.
Cinnabar should be ground with the juices of nimbuka and dried over fire.
Then, treated in that way with rice-water, it becomes purified.
Purified cinnabar removes erysipelas, skin disease, itching, and poison.
It promotes the knitting of fractures, cleanses wounds, and heals them.
Samudraphena is beneficial for the eyes, scraping, cooling, and flowing.
It removes ear discharge, pain, and filth, and it digests and kindles appetite.
When impure, it causes breaking pain in the limbs; therefore it should be purified.
Samudraphena, when thoroughly ground with nimbu-water, becomes purified.

children.text: gairikaṃ kiṃcid ājyena bhṛṣṭaṃ śuddhaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: Gairika, fried a little with ghee, becomes purified.
It produces bodily complexion, firmness of age, strength, and increase of vital energy.
It removes prameha, skin disease, eruptions, all wounds, and poison.
But golden gairika is superior to ordinary gairika.
For the seeds of gandharvahasta, with coconut water,
purification occurs in one yāma; dantī seed should be cooked in the same way.
Pepper, steeped in sour buttermilk for three ghaṭikās,

children.text: marīcaṃ nistuṣaṃ kṛtvā śuddhaṃ bhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: when stripped of its husk, certainly becomes purified.
Vaidehī should be steeped in citraka juices in a covered vessel in the sun.
There it becomes properly purified; it should be used in mercurial preparations.
Rāmaṭha, they know, is steeped for a yāma in lotus-leaf juice in the sun.
It obtains purification and should be used in mercurial preparations.
Conch-shell is alkaline, cooling, absorbent, and destroys grahaṇī disorder and purging.
It removes eye growths, improves complexion, and dispels youthful pimples.

children.text: aśuddho guṇado naiṣa śuddho'mlaiḥ sa guṇapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When impure it does not give its virtues; when purified with sour substances it gives its virtues.
The right-spiralled conch destroys the three doṣas, is pure, and is a treasure.
It remedies seizures, misfortune, wasting disease, kṣveḍa poison, emaciation, bitter disorders, consumption, and disability.
Copper, bhūbhava, and nāga should be ground, thirty parts of them, in equal quantity,
with purā, lac, spider-web, fish-oil-cake, and ṭaṅkaṇa.
Having combined them with these liquids and triturated them, one should blow them well in the furnace.
Even peacock feathers give off an essence like copper.
The essence of bhūnāga is cooling and dispels all skin diseases and wounds.
By drinking water infused with it, both fixed and moving
poison is destroyed; mercury placed in a vessel made of it becomes firm from fire.
The same property is considered to belong also to the essence arising from peacock feathers.
In cow's milk, decoction of triphalā, and juice of bhṛṅga, in equal parts,
one should triturate camphor for one yāma; it obtains purification.
Impure ṭaṅkaṇa, when used, causes vomiting and dizziness.
Therefore it should be purified in this way: soaked in cow-dung, it becomes clean.
Ṭaṅkaṇa kindles fire, purifies gold and silver, and is flowing.
It removes poison-doṣa, is pleasant to the heart, and dispels disorders of vāta and śleṣman.
Kālakūṭa, vatsanābha, and śṛṅgaka are stimulants.
Hālāhala, brahmaputra, haridra, and saktuka likewise,

children.text: saurāṣṭrika iti proktā viṣabhedā amī nava ||
children.translated_text: and saurāṣṭrika: these are said to be the nine kinds of poison.
Among them the brāhmaṇa is pale, the kṣatriya is red in color,

children.text: vaiśyaḥ pītaprabhaḥ śūdraḥ kṛṣṇābhaḥ sa tu ninditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the vaiśya is yellowish in appearance, and the śūdra is blackish; that one is condemned.

children.text: rasāyane viṣaṃ vipraṃ dehapuṣṭau tu bāhujam
children.translated_text: In rasāyana one should use the brāhmaṇa poison, and for nourishing the body the bāhuja one.
