children.text: kuṣṭhanāśe prayuñjīta vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ tu dhātuṣu ||
children.translated_text: For destroying skin disease one should use the vaiśya; the śūdra should be used for metals.
Poison takes life, but when properly applied it gives life and is a rasāyana.
It is an excellent yogavāhin, removes śleṣman and vāta, and conquers sannipāta.

children.text: viṣaṃ tu khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā vastrakhaṇḍena bandhayet
children.translated_text: Poison should be cut into pieces and tied up in a piece of cloth.
It should be placed in cow's urine and kept in the sun for three days.

children.text: gomūtraṃ tu pradātavyaṃ nūtanaṃ pratyahaṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Fresh cow's urine should be supplied each day by the learned.
When the three days have passed, one should take it out, dry it, and grind it gently.

children.text: śudhyatyevaṃ viṣaṃ sevyaṃ yogyaṃ bhavati cārtijit ||
children.translated_text: In this way poison is purified, becomes fit to be administered, and conquers affliction.
Having broken poison into pieces and tied it in cloth, by means of a dolā apparatus,
it obtains purification after one yāma when steamed in goat's milk.
A poison nodule should be placed in buffalo dung and sealed firmly.
One should cook it for a yāma in a dung fire; when filtered through cloth, the poison is clean.

children.text: kaṇaśo vatsanābhaṃ ca kṛtvā baddhvā ca karpaṭe
children.translated_text: Vatsanābha too, made into particles and tied in a rag,
in a dolā apparatus with water and milk, obtains purification after one prahara.
Poison combined with an equal amount of ṭaṅkaṇa and twice as much uṣaṇa

children.text: viṣaṃ saṃyojitaṃ śuddhaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavati sarvathā ||
children.translated_text: becomes purified and completely killed in every respect.
Poison is a rasāyana, strengthening, and dispels disorders of vāta and śleṣman.
It is pungent, bitter, and astringent, intoxicating, and gives ease.
It is diffusive, removes cold, is heating, and destroys skin disease, vāta, and blood disorders.
It destroys weak digestion, dyspnea, cough, spleen disease, abdominal swelling, and fistula,
as well as gulma, pallor, wounds, and hemorrhoids, successively in men.
Gaurīpāṣāṇaka is said to be of two kinds, white and red.
The white is like a conch; the red is declared to resemble a pomegranate.
The white is said to be artificial, while the red is mountain-born.
Both bear the form of poison and are esteemed in mercurial operations.
There is another gaurīpāṣāṇaka, harsh, a red powder.
It causes the binding of mercury, is unctuous, removes doṣas, and gives potency to mercury.

children.text: ghananādarasānvite ca mallaḥ paripācyaḥ kila dolakāhvayantre
children.translated_text: Malla, together with ghananāda juice, is indeed to be thoroughly cooked in the apparatus called dolā.

children.text: śubhavahniratho dinaṃ ca mandaḥ parideyaḥ parijāyate sa śuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a good fire for a day, and afterwards a gentle one, should be applied all around; it is produced purified.
The purification of ullīpāṣāṇa, as approved by the śāstra, will be stated.
Having powdered it and tied it in cloth, together with water of śilākṣāra,

children.text: dolāyantre dinaikaṃ tu pācitaḥ śuddhim āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: it should be cooked for one day in a dolā apparatus; then it obtains purification.
Having tied vikaṭa in a bundle, with the dolā apparatus in kāñjika,

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇe vā gavāṃ dugdhe pācayed ghaṭikādvayam
children.translated_text: or in borax, or in cow's milk, one should cook it for two ghaṭikās.
Or in goat-meat broth; it certainly becomes purified.
Some know ullī, pāṣāṇa, and malla as alternative names.

children.text: vāte kaphe tathā śīte yojayanti cikitsakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Physicians apply it in vāta, kapha, and cold conditions.
Arka latex, snuhī latex, lāṅgalī, karavīra,
guñjā, ahiphena, and dhattūra are the seven classes of <s>upaviṣa</s> (secondary poisons).
Arka, snuhī, lāṅgalī, guñjā, hayāri, viṣamuṣṭi,
dhūrta, ahiphena, and jaipāla are the nine classes of <s>upaviṣa</s>.
The two arkas are fluid, and remove vāta, skin disease, itching, and poison.
They destroy spleen disease, abdominal tumors, piles, liver disease, phlegmatic abdominal swelling, and worms.
Sehuṇḍa is purgative, sharp, digestive, pungent, and heavy.
It destroys colic, a hard lump, distension, abdominal tumor, swelling, abdominal disease, and disorders of wind.
It destroys the doṣas, liver and spleen disorders, skin disease, madness, stones, and pallor.
The milk of arka and sehuṇḍa is said to be naturally purified.
Lāṅgalī attains purification when kept for a day in cow urine.
Kalikārī is fluid and conquers skin disease, swelling, piles, wounds, and pain.
It is sharp, hot, worm-destroying, light, bilious, and abortifacient.
Guñjā, steamed in kāñjika, attains purification within a yāma.
Guñjā is light, cooling, dry, breaking, and conquers dyspnea and cough.
It is mildly warm, aphrodisiac, and removes skin disease, itching, phlegm, bile, and wounds.
Hayāri is to be purified like poison, by a dolā in cow's milk.
The two karavīras remove eye disease, skin disease, and wounds.
They are light, hot, and destroy worms and itching; when eaten they are regarded as poisonous.
Viṣamuṣṭi becomes purified when slightly smeared with ghee.
Viṣamuṣṭi is bitter, pungent, sharp, hot, and removes phlegm and vāta.
It is remembered as removing dog poison and madness, and as causing intoxication.
Jaipāla is heavy and bitter, causes vomiting, and removes fever and skin disease.
It is hot, fluid, and removes wounds, phlegm, itching, worms, and poison.

children.text: jaipālaṃ rahitaṃ tvagaṅkurarasajñābhir male māhiṣe nikṣiptaṃ tryahamuṣṇatoyavimale khalve savāsorditam
children.translated_text: Jaipāla, stripped of its skin, sprouts, juice, and kernel, placed for three days in buffalo dung and pure hot water, and pounded in a mortar with cloth,

children.text: liptaṃ nūtanakharpareṣu vigatasnehaṃ rajaḥsaṃnibhaṃ nimbūkāmbuvibhāvitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ śuddhaṃ guṇāḍhyaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: smeared on new potsherds until free of oil and like dust, and repeatedly impregnated with lemon water, becomes purified and rich in virtues.

children.text: jaipālaṃ nistuṣaṃ kṛtvā dugdhe dolāyutaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: Having removed the husk from jaipāla, one should cook it in milk in a dolā apparatus.
After rejecting the inner tongue, one should use it in mercury operations.

children.text: vastre baddhvā tu jaipālaṃ gomayasyodake nyaset
children.translated_text: Having tied jaipāla in cloth, one should place it in water from cow dung.
One should cook it for the duration of a yāma; jaipāla then goes to purification.
Dhattūra seed, after staying in cow urine for four yāmas,

children.text: kvathitaṃ nistuṣaṃ kṛtvā śuddhaṃ yāgeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: is boiled and stripped of its husk; when purified, it should be used in preparations.
Dhattūra produces intoxication, color, digestive fire, and vāta, and removes fever and skin disease.
It is hot and heavy, and removes wounds, phlegm, itching, worms, and poison.
Ahiphena should be impregnated twenty-one times with ginger juice.
It is purified; in the stated preparations one should apply it according to that rule.
Aphuka is drying, constipating, phlegm-destroying, and increases vāta and pitta.
It causes intoxication, thirst, burning, obstruction of semen, exhaustion, and bewilderment.
In diarrhea and grahaṇī disease it is beneficial, kindling digestion and cooking the food.
When used for some days it causes dizziness; otherwise it causes pain.
Mercury, triturated with the nine, becomes with its wings cut off.

children.text: mukhaṃ ca jāyate tasya dhātūṃśca grasatetarām ||
children.translated_text: Its mouth is produced, and it then consumes metals very greatly.

children.text: bhaṅgikā pittalā tiktā tīkṣṇoṣṇā grāhiṇī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: Bhaṅgikā is bilious, bitter, sharp, hot, constipating, and light.
It emaciates, kindles digestion, is appetizing, causes intoxication, and removes kapha and vāta.
One should steam bhaṅgā with a decoction of babbūla bark and dry it.
After giving it an impregnation with cow's milk, one should use it, dried, everywhere.

children.text: oṃ namaḥ pracaṇḍagaruḍāya pakṣirājāya viṣṇuvāhanāya vinatāsutāya he garuḍa kaśyapasuta vainateya tārkṣya svarṇavajra cañcuvajra tuṇḍanakhapraharaṇāyānantavāsukitakṣakakarkoṭapadmamahāpadmaśaṅkhapālakulikajayavijayāṣṭamahānāgakāla uccāṭanīmūṣakaviṣapraharaṇāvahananadhūnana śīghrakampa 2 ḍhaṇḍhara he he śrīgaruḍāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to fierce <s>Garuḍa</s>, king of birds, vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, son of <s>Vinatā</s>. O <s>Garuḍa</s>, son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, golden-thunderbolt, thunderbolt-beaked, with beak, nails, and weapons, expeller of <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Karkoṭa</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, <s>Kulika</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, and <s>Vijaya</s>, the eight great nāgas and Kāla; striker, summoner, and shaker of mouse poison; quick trembler, quick trembler; ḍhaṇḍhara, he he, homage to glorious <s>Garuḍa</s>.
With this mantra, one who knows mantras should take water equal to a small mouthful.
After reciting over it seven times, he should make one whose consciousness has been seized drink it.
Through the force of poison from snakes and the like, he at once obtains freedom from poison.
In this way water should be drunk only three times; it should not be drunk further.
That water should indeed be thrown into the middle of his mouth.
Or the wise man should strike him on the head with the forefinger,

children.text: trivāraṃ mantrapūrvaṃ tu nirviṣo bhavati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: three times, preceded by the mantra; he becomes free of poison in an instant.
One should impregnate powdered mica for one day with kāñjika,
and mix it well with waters produced from plantain and sūraṇa, and with radishes.
Again, with one fourth part borax and with small fish in equal amount,
having mixed them with buffalo dung, one should then make pellets of it.
One should blow it strongly with a harsh fire; it releases an essence like bronze.
When killed, one should consume mica with mercury as one would copper.
The essence of mica is cooling, removes the three doṣas, and is a rasāyana.
In particular it produces virility and is supreme for arresting age.
Mica placed in sūraṇa and rubbed with the expressed juice of agastya leaves,
kept in a cowshed for a month, becomes like mercury.
Lac, rājī, sesame, śigru, borax, salt, and jaggery,
mixed with half as much tālaka, in a crucible, in a firm vessel,

children.text: ruddhvā puṭed adhoyantre satvaṃ muñcati sarvathā ||
children.translated_text: sealed and heated in a lower apparatus, releases its essence completely.
One should kindle the dried wood of the kṣāra-tree in fire.

children.text: nītvā tadbhasma mṛtpātre kṣiptvā nīre caturguṇe ||
children.translated_text: Having taken that ash into an earthen vessel, one should throw it into four times as much water.
After rubbing it, one should keep it overnight; in the morning one should draw off the clear water.
One should boil that water over fire until it has all dried up.
Then, having taken it out from the vessel, the alkali, white in appearance, is to be collected.
It should be like powder, fit for rubbing on; the metallic one remains as a decoction does.
Thus the wise man should apply the two alkalis in suitable operations.
